prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1116; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers were dispatched to a sideswipe collision in League City, Texas, involving two vehicles. According to both drivers, Driver 2 was changing lanes when the right side of that vehicle contacted the left side of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 was seated in the vehicle at the time, and I observed Driver 1 at the scene along with a Passenger. Driver 1 reported a wrist fracture and said the impact threw the arm against the door frame. That injury is consistent with the type and force of the contact. Damage to both vehicles lines up with the described impact. Scene photographs show some of the reported positions, though no independent witnesses came forward. A few older scratches appear on the damaged panel, and some may predate this collision. Driver 1 produced insurance documents listing Driver 1 as the named insured on the policy. Neither driver was cited. Both vehicles were towed from the scene.
